**Nine of the thirty-four log calls never fire.** Six `debug` and three `info`, including the one in `sources/marc.py` that records a record `mrrc` could not parse — added specifically so that a malformed SRU response would not be silent, and currently silent. `sources/covers.py` accounts for most of the rest: whether a cover was found, why one was skipped, whether a record had no identifiers to try.

**The other twenty-five reach Python's last-resort handler**, which writes the bare message to stderr with no timestamp, no logger name and no level. `ingest/ocr.py` distinguishes six failure modes — an API error, an unexpected error, a truncated reply, a refused image, a missing text block, a reply that is not schema-constrained JSON — and an administrator debugging a failed scan sees six unlabelled sentences.

## What to add

A `LOGGING` dict with a console handler and a formatter that carries at least the timestamp, level and logger name. Application loggers at `DEBUG` when `DEBUG` is true and `INFO` otherwise; the third-party loggers that are noisy at `DEBUG` — `httpx` in particular, which logs every request — held at `WARNING` regardless.

Django's own `LOGGING` default is a merge rather than a replacement unless `disable_existing_loggers` says otherwise, so check what survives rather than assuming the dict is the whole configuration.

## What not to add yet

`structlog` is the right direction and the wrong time.

It is the right direction because it composes with the standard library instead of replacing it. Django, `httpx`, `anthropic` and `mrrc` all log through stdlib, and structlog is designed to share stdlib's handlers so every log line goes through one pipeline and comes out in one format. `loguru` has the nicer API and replaces stdlib, which means an intercept shim to capture Django's own logging and a `LOGGING` setting that no longer does anything. For a Django application that is friction without a compensating benefit.

It is the wrong time because the payoff for structured logging is querying it — filter by record, group failures by source catalog, count OCR calls per day. That needs somewhere to aggregate into, and there is no deployment. Until then the entire benefit is JSON in a terminal, which is worse to read than formatted text for the one person reading it.

Every call site already uses lazy `%s` interpolation rather than f-strings, which is both correct stdlib practice and what structlog's stdlib integration expects, so adopting it later costs no rewrite of call sites. Keep it that way.

## The question worth deciding alongside

The log lines interpolate ISBNs, record identifiers and search queries. On one person's laptop that is nothing. On a shared host it is the same question the discarded-scan work asked about photographs: what is retained, where it goes, and for how long. Decide it when production settings are written rather than discovering it in a log file.

## Verification

`logger.debug` in `sources/marc.py` produces a line when `DEBUG` is true and does not when it is false. A failed OCR call produces a line naming `ingest.ocr` and its level. `httpx` does not log a line per request at `DEBUG`. The check that matters is running the application and reading the output, not a unit test asserting on a handler list.
close_reason: Logging configuration landed in 840f921; the django and django.request loggers are covered by bd-n7a.1

title: Cluster cataloging practices from field co-occurrence
description:
The survey in `docs/marc-in-practice.md` counts fields one at a time. That answers "how often does 730 appear" and not "what does a record carrying 730 also carry", and the second question is the one that would let otzar recognise a treatment rather than a field.

The set-and-volume work assumes a taxonomy of treatments — series treatment, multipart monograph, uniform title, analytic, set record with contents — taken from the format documentation and from talking to catalogers. It has never been checked against records. Field co-occurrence would check it: cluster records on which fields and subfields they carry, and see whether the clusters correspond to the treatments the taxonomy names.

Three outcomes, and all three are worth having:

The clusters match the taxonomy, which confirms it and gives each treatment a detectable signature otzar can test a record against.

The clusters cut across the taxonomy, which says the treatments are a cataloger's vocabulary rather than a property of records, and that otzar should classify on evidence rather than on a named type.

The clusters correspond to the cataloging agency or the decade rather than to anything bibliographic, which would say the variation is institutional, and that knowing where a record came from predicts more than reading it does.

## What it needs first

**A larger and differently-drawn sample.** The existing corpus is 1,027 records reached by title searches for works named in advance, which finds records catalogued under those titles and misses the ones expressing the same work differently. Clustering that sample would mostly recover the shape of the queries.

Draw the next one along axes that do not presuppose the answer: by date range, by publisher, by subject heading, by language of the record, by cataloging agency in `040`. Include material that is not a multi-volume set, since a classifier that has only ever seen sets cannot tell that it is looking at one.

**A record-level feature representation**, which is more than tag presence: indicator values, which subfields are present within a field, whether a linked alternate script exists, and the two dates from `008`.

## Scope

This is a study, not a feature. Its output is a written finding in `docs/` and, if the clusters turn out to be real, a description of each signature precise enough to implement. Nothing in the application changes on the strength of it without a separate ticket.

Worth doing before the identity rules in the set work are written, since the whole question there is which evidence establishes that two records describe one set.
close_reason: done

title: Record author roles from MARC relator terms and codes
description:
The record-to-author link holds only a record id and an author id, so a translator, an editor and the author of the original text all attach to a record identically. The catalog page lists them side by side as if all stood in the same relation to the book.

This is the half of otzar-55i that was not built. The other half — transcribing 245`$c`, the statement of responsibility — landed already and covers the common case in prose: "translated, annotated, and elucidated by Yisrael Isser Zvi Herczeg ; in collaboration with Yaakov Petroff". That answers "who did what" for a reader. It does not give the catalog structured roles it can browse or filter on.

## What the data actually supports

MARC carries roles in `700$e` (relator term, e.g. "translator") and `700$4` (relator code, e.g. `trl`), both optional and both frequently absent. The LC record quoted in otzar-55i has four `700` fields and neither subfield on any of them, which is exactly why the roles there exist only in the `$c` prose. NLI records carry relators more often.

So the ceiling on this work is what the catalogs supply. Build it for the records that have relators, leave the rest unroled, and do not attempt to parse roles out of `$c` prose — otzar-55i rules that out explicitly, and it is a trap: the prose is free text in two scripts with no controlled vocabulary behind it.

## Shape

A role field on the through table between `Record` and `Author`. `Record.authors` is a plain `ManyToManyField` today, so this means an explicit `through` model, a schema migration, and a data migration for existing links — not simply an added column.

`sources/marc.py` reads `700` fields and keeps only the name; it needs to carry the relator term and code alongside each additional author, and `_attach_from_candidate` needs to store them.

The `$4` codes come from the MARC Relator Code list and need mapping to display terms. Prefer the code where both are present: `$e` is free text and varies in capitalisation and punctuation between catalogs.

Decide what an unroled author displays as. "Author" is a guess that will sometimes be wrong; showing nothing is honest but makes roled and unroled authors look inconsistent on the same page.

## Sequencing

Touches `catalog/models.py` and a migration, `sources/marc.py`, `ingest/views.py` and the record detail page — four files that other work contends for. Worth picking up when those are quiet rather than forcing it alongside them.

title: Tell a publisher's imprint apart from a multi-volume work
description:
`490 $a` and `830 $a` carry two different kinds of thing, and otzar treats them as one. A survey of 122 records from NLI and LC, written up in `docs/marc-in-practice.md`, found these as the most frequent values:

```
  8  Talmud Bavli
  5  ArtScroll series
  4  ArtScroll Series
  3  The ArtScroll series
  3  מקראות גדולות
  2  Judaica books of the Prophets
  2  Studia Judaica (Walter de Gruyter & Co.)
  1  Miqraot gedolot
```

`Talmud Bavli` and `מקראות גדולות` are works with volumes somebody sets out to complete. Volume 3 of Miqraot Gedolot is a thing a collector wants and can be missing. `ArtScroll series` and `Studia Judaica` are publishers' labels attached to books with nothing else in common. Nobody holds volume 3 of ArtScroll, and nobody has a gap in it.

`create_series_volumes` makes a `Series` from whichever of these a confirmed record happened to carry. In a frum collection, where a large fraction of the English-language holdings are ArtScroll, that files hundreds of unrelated books into one row and gives each of them a position in a sequence that does not exist. The series page for it is noise, the gap placeholders are meaningless, and the per-volume lookup that fills gaps would go looking for volumes of a publisher.

## What separates them

There is no subfield that says which kind a series statement is, so this is inference from several weak signals rather than a lookup:

**Numbering.** A work-set numbers its volumes and the numbers run without gaps. An imprint either has no `$v` at all or has one that counts books published rather than parts of a work. `ArtScroll series` in the corpus carries no `$v`; `פרסומי האגודה לחקר תולדות היהודים ; $v 51` carries a high one, which is a monographic series rather than a set — the third kind, and the one that most resembles an imprint in practice.

**A uniform title that matches.** A set that is a work has a `130` or `240` naming that work, and its parts appear in `$p`. `Talmud Bavli` as a series statement alongside `130 $a Talmud Bavli. $p Pesahim` is one work seen twice. An imprint never matches a uniform title, because it is not a work.

**The publisher.** An imprint's name usually contains or is the publisher's, and the same publisher appears on every record carrying it. That is cheap to check against the `260`/`264` already parsed.

**Breadth of subject.** A work-set's volumes share a subject; an imprint's do not. This is the weakest signal and the most expensive, and it is listed for completeness rather than as a recommendation.

## What to do with the answer

Do not silently drop imprint series. The information is real and belongs in the record — a person browsing for ArtScroll editions is asking a reasonable question — but it is a publication fact rather than a set membership, and it should not create a `Series` with volumes and gaps.

Whether that means two models, or one model with a kind, or an imprint being an attribute of a record rather than an entity, is the decision this ticket makes. The constraint is that a gap placeholder must never be created for something nobody can complete.

## Getting it wrong should be recoverable

The signals are weak and a collection will contain cases none of them settle. Whatever classifies a series statement has to be correctable by a person, and the correction has to survive the next record that arrives claiming otherwise — the same requirement the rest of the set work has, for the same reason.

## Tests

A record carrying `490 $a ArtScroll series` with no `$v` and no matching uniform title does not produce a set with volume positions. A record carrying `490 $a Talmud Bavli` alongside `130 $a Talmud Bavli. $p Pesahim` does. Two records from the same publisher carrying the same imprint do not become volumes of each other. A person's correction of either classification survives a subsequent record that disagrees.
close_reason: done

title: Cross-device OCR progress e2e test races on a loaded runner
description:
`tests/e2e/test_title_page_handoff.py::TestSharedOCRProgress::test_desktop_sees_reading_while_phone_runs_ocr` fails intermittently in CI and passes on rerun. It has cost at least one rerun already.

The test proves the OCR lease is visible to a second device: the phone starts a run, and the desktop's poll must show the disabled "Reading..." button. The timings are a mocked OCR call that sleeps 6 seconds, a desktop poll every 3 seconds, and an assertion allowing 8 seconds for the state to appear.

That leaves roughly two poll cycles of headroom, which is enough on an idle machine and not enough on a loaded GitHub runner where the browser, the live server and the poll all contend. Nothing about the behaviour under test is wrong; the margin is.

## Shape

Do not simply raise the timeout — that trades a flake for a slow suite and hides the next regression behind an even longer wait. Prefer making the test wait on the thing it cares about rather than on wall-clock time: the lease is a database row, so the desktop's view of it is deterministic once the poll fires, and the poll interval is the only real variable.

Options worth weighing: drive the poll explicitly rather than waiting for its timer; shorten the poll interval under test; or hold the mocked OCR open on an event the test releases, so the run lasts exactly as long as the assertions need instead of a fixed six seconds. The last is the most faithful to what is being tested and removes the race entirely rather than widening it.

Check whether the sibling test `test_second_device_is_told_ocr_is_already_running` shares the same shape; it uses the same 6-second sleep and would race the same way.

comments.author: dchud
comments.text: Reopened: Recurred at a different point. #116's first CI e2e run (run 35810615492, attempt 1) failed in test_desktop_sees_reading_while_phone_runs_ocr with 'the phone's request never reached the vision call; the phone got back nothing': the assert ocr_reached.wait(timeout=15) at tests/e2e/test_title_page_handoff.py:884 timed out, so the phone's Run OCR request did not reach the mocked OCR call within 15 s. The desktop-poll race this bead fixed is not what failed. main's CI was green, the test passed 3 of 3 runs locally, and a rerun passed. Check what the phone request is waiting on before it reaches the view (lease acquisition, the live server's request handling under load) rather than raising the 15 s bound.

title: Populate romanized subject and series headings from both multiscript mechanisms
description:
`Subject.heading_romanized` and `Series.title_romanized` exist and nothing fills them. `parse_record` in `sources/marc.py` resolves 880 linkage only for 245 (title) and 100 (author) through `_linked_880_value`; the 650 subject loop and the 490/830 series extraction read the primary field alone. An LC record for a Hebrew book therefore yields romanized subjects with no Hebrew form, and the subject browse page shows one heading twice in two scripts from two sources.

## There are two mechanisms and 880 is only one of them

A survey of 122 records, written up in `docs/marc-in-practice.md`, found that the two catalogs express parallel scripts in entirely different ways.

LC uses 880. Fifteen of its 41 records carry alternate graphic representation fields, linked through `$6` to 245, 246, 100, 240, 260, 264, 700, 710, 505, 730 and 740.

NLI uses none at all — zero 880s in 81 records. It marks the script on the field itself with `$9 heb` or `$9 lat` and links the parallel forms with `$8 PreferredLanguageHeading`, on 78 of those 81 records:

```
130 0# $a Talmud Bavli. $p Pesahim. $l English. $9 lat $8 PreferredLanguageHeading
130 0# $a משנה. $p פרה. $f תשע"ו $9 heb $8 PreferredLanguageHeading
```

So extending 880 resolution alone fixes the LC half and reads nothing from the endpoint that holds the Hebrew material. The two are different shapes as well as different tags: 880 is a pointer from one field to another, `$9`/`$8` is a label on each of several sibling fields that have to be grouped.

NLI also carries the cross-script variant in `246`, with `$i` giving the display phrase:

```
246 1# $i בשער גם: $a ערוך השלחן
```

against a romanized 245. A reader looking only at 245 concludes the record has one script.

## Scope

Read both mechanisms wherever a romanized or Hebrew alternate is wanted: 650 subjects, 490/830 series, and the 246 variant title. Return the alternate alongside the primary rather than choosing between them, carry it on the candidate dict, and store it on confirm in `_attach_from_candidate` and the series persistence path.

Matching a subject or series by either script form belongs with this change so the two forms merge into one row; the subject deduplication that landed with subdivision handling is the place to add it, and `find_matching_series` the place for series. `מקראות גדולות` and `Miqraot gedolot` appear in the survey as separate series values for one work, with NLI having already marked them as parallel forms — the evidence for the merge is in the record and unread.

## Tests

An LC record with an 880 linked to a 650 yields both forms. An NLI record with parallel 650s marked `$9 heb` and `$9 lat` yields both forms, and does so with no 880 present. A record with only one script yields one form and no empty alternate. Two records expressing one subject in different scripts resolve to a single `Subject` row, and the same for `Series`.

title: Build and publish the documentation with Material for MkDocs
description:
`CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` both name Material for MkDocs as this project's documentation tool. There is no `mkdocs.yml`, nothing builds a site, and `docs/` is plain Markdown read on GitHub or in a terminal. The claim has been false since it was written.

The resolution is to make it true rather than to delete it. The documentation has grown past the point where a directory of Markdown files serves a reader well: a user guide, an administration guide, a development guide and a survey of how three catalogs express MARC, with no index, no search across them, and no ordering except alphabetical by filename.

## What it needs

A `mkdocs.yml` with the Material theme and an explicit `nav`, so the ordering is a decision rather than a directory listing. An `index.md` for the site root; `README.md` covers what the project is and duplicating it wholesale is worse than writing a short entry page that points into the guides.

`docs/plans/` stays out of the built site. Those are working artifacts exempt from the persistent-artifact rules, dense with bead IDs and time-state wording, and publishing them would put the least durable writing in the project in front of the most casual reader.

`just docs` to serve locally with live reload, and a build target that fails on a broken internal link rather than publishing one. MkDocs has a strict mode for exactly that, and it is worth enabling from the start: the cost of turning it on later is fixing every link at once.

## Publishing

Build and deploy to GitHub Pages from a workflow on push to `main`. Deploying with the Pages actions rather than committing to a `gh-pages` branch keeps generated output out of the repository's history.

The workflow needs `pages: write` and `id-token: write`, which is more than the existing CI job holds. Grant those on the deploy job alone and leave everything else at `contents: read` — the zizmor work is about to make that pattern the standard here rather than the exception.

Enabling Pages and setting its source to GitHub Actions is a repository setting, not a file, so it has to be done by hand once before the first deploy succeeds.

## Rendering

The documentation contains Hebrew, Cyrillic, and tables mixing right-to-left and left-to-right text in the same row. Check the built pages rather than assuming: a survey of Hebrew cataloging practice that renders its examples backwards is worse than one nobody publishes.

## What this closes

Two of the three drift items this was filed alongside have already been fixed: `pymarc` is out of `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, and `docs/administration.md` gives the correct `CLAUDE_MODEL` default. The MkDocs claim is the last one standing.

## Verification

`just docs-build` produces a site with every page in the nav reachable and no broken internal links, and fails when one is introduced. `docs/plans/` does not appear in the output. The published site loads, its search returns results from every guide, and the Hebrew and Cyrillic examples render in the correct direction.
close_reason: done

title: Add a DNB cascade to the title-page search
description:
`run_cascade` in `sources/cascade.py` runs the NLI and LC step lists; DNB is queried only in `isbn_lookup`. A title-page photograph of a German or Yiddish book reaches two catalogs that hold little of that material and skips the one that does. The cascade is data: a `DNB_CASCADE` list of `(name, CQL template)` pairs in DNB's index vocabulary, and a `search_dnb` wrapper, make it a third source rendered by the same candidate partial. Confirm the index names against DNB's SRU explain response before writing the templates.

Worth doing when a DNB-held book fails the title-page path. The one DNB record in the catalog arrived through ISBN.

title: Constrain OCR output with a response schema
description:
`extract_metadata_from_image` asks for JSON in the prompt text and then repairs whatever comes back. `_parse_vision_json` strips markdown fences, and when parsing fails it rewrites any double quote sitting between two Hebrew characters as a gershayim (U+05F4) and tries again. A quote that lands anywhere else — beside a Latin letter, a digit, a space, or punctuation — still fails, `extract_metadata_from_image` returns None, and the user sees "OCR could not extract metadata" for a photo the model read correctly.

Hebrew title pages carry gershayim constantly (רש״י, תשע״ד), so this is a routine failure, not an edge case.

Structured outputs remove the failure class: constrain the response to a JSON schema covering the eight metadata keys. The fence stripping, the gershayim repair, and the None-on-unparseable path all go away, and a genuine extraction failure becomes distinguishable from a serialization accident. Check the current API shape against the `claude-api` skill rather than writing the request from memory.

The remaining model-id cleanup is in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which sets `CLAUDE_MODEL=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` in two places. Current ids are unsuffixed.

`ingest/ocr.py` and `.env.example` no longer need attention: the default is already `claude-sonnet-5` and the per-scan costs were refreshed alongside it.
close_reason: Merged in PR #15

title: A failed OCR re-run discards the previous extraction
description:
`run_ocr` accepts `pending` scans so the user can re-run against the
same image. On `metadata is None` it sets `ocr_output = None` and
reverts status to `awaiting_ocr` unconditionally.

So: the user has usable metadata on screen, presses "Re-run OCR" hoping
for a better read, the vision call fails transiently or returns
unparseable JSON, and the extraction they already had is gone. The edit
form is replaced by the error partial and there is no way back to it.

This is current intended behaviour --
`test_run_ocr_failure_after_success_resets_to_awaiting` asserts it, with
the rationale that the queue card should surface the scan again. The
question is whether that rationale outweighs destroying a good result on
a transient failure.

Suggested: only overwrite `ocr_output` on success, and leave a scan that
was already `pending` in `pending`. The failure notice can offer both
"Try again" and "Keep the previous result". That test would change to
assert the previous output survives.

Found in review of PR #7. Needs a decision before implementing, since it
reverses a deliberate choice.
close_reason: done

title: Connect the response cache, API usage log and search reindex paths
description:
Three pieces of infrastructure exist with unit tests and nothing calls them: `ResponseCache` in `sources/cache.py` (a 30-day file cache keyed on URL and parameters), `APIUsageLog` in `ingest/models.py` (an OCR cost table with an admin page and no writers), and `reindex_all` in `catalog/search.py` (invoked only by `load_test_data`). A fourth gap sits beside them: records edited or deleted through the Django admin bypass `index_record`, so the FTS index goes stale with no signal.

Each child is small and independent of the others. Together they connect parts of the system that are written but not running.
close_reason: All three children closed

title: Wire ResponseCache into the SRU and VIAF clients
description:
`SRUClient.search` in `sources/sru.py` sleeps for the polite delay and calls `httpx.get` on every invocation. `ResponseCache` in `sources/cache.py` offers `get(base_url, params)` and `set(...)` over Django's file cache with a 30-day TTL, and nothing calls it. A repeated title-page search replays every cascade step against NLI and LC with a three-second delay per step, so re-running a search that already ran costs twenty seconds or more and the same load on the source catalogs.

Check the cache before the delay and the request; store the raw XML on success only, so a transient failure is retried rather than remembered. Apply the same to `sources/viaf.py`. The cache directory is `DATA_DIR/cache`, already configured. Add tests that a second identical `search` call makes no HTTP request; pytest-socket blocks the network in tests, so the assertion is that the cached call succeeds where an uncached one raises.

The series claim work fans out one search per volume; with caching, a retried or reopened claim costs nothing at the source catalogs.
close_reason: Merged in PR #41

title: Add a reindex management command and index records saved through the admin
description:
`index_record` is called from the ingest views when a record is created or edited, and from nowhere else. `RecordAdmin` in `catalog/admin.py` has no `save_model` or `delete_model` override and no signal handler exists, so a record edited in the admin keeps its old text in the FTS index and one deleted in the admin leaves an orphaned index row. Author, subject and publisher text is denormalized into the index, so renaming an author in the admin leaves every one of that author's records stale too. `reindex_all` exists in `catalog/search.py` and only `load_test_data` calls it; an operator has no command to recover with.

Two parts. A `reindex` management command that calls `ensure_fts_table` and `reindex_all` and reports a count. And index maintenance on admin writes: either `post_save`/`post_delete` handlers on `Record`, on its M2M through tables and on the related models (so a renamed author reindexes its records), or explicit `save_model`/`delete_model` overrides on each ModelAdmin. Handlers cover every write path including future ones; overrides are explicit and easier to read. Pick one and apply it to every model the index reads from.

Tests: edit a record through the admin client and search for the new title; delete through the admin and confirm the index row is gone; run the command against a database with a dropped FTS table and confirm every record is searchable afterwards.
close_reason: Merged in PR #37

title: Log OCR calls to APIUsageLog and enforce a daily scan limit
description:
`APIUsageLog` in `ingest/models.py` has fields for api, model, user and input and output tokens, a migration and an admin page, and no code writes to it. `extract_metadata` in `ingest/ocr.py` receives the Anthropic `message` object, whose `usage` carries the token counts, and discards it. The admin page for OCR cost is therefore always empty, and nothing limits how many scans a user or a day can run.

Write one row per OCR call from `run_ocr`, which knows the user and the scan, with the model name, token counts and whether the call produced a reading. `extract_metadata` returns only the parsed dict, so either return the usage alongside it or log from inside the function with the caller passing the user. Add a configurable daily cap on OCR calls (an env var with a generous default) that `run_ocr` checks before calling the API and names in the failure partial when exceeded, so a retry loop on a phone cannot spend without bound.
close_reason: done

title: Say what problem the MARC survey is about, and how its sample is skewed
description:
`docs/marc-in-practice.md` opens by saying that the catalogs send something different from what the specification predicts. It never says what question the document exists to answer, so a reader meets a hundred lines of field frequencies before learning why anyone counted them.

The question is the multi-volume set. A collection of Judaica is full of works that arrive in many physical volumes — a Talmud in eighteen, a Mishnah Berurah in six — and otzar has to decide, for each incoming record, which set it belongs to and which volume it is. Every measurement in the document exists to answer that, and the ones that matter most are the absences: the fields a reader of the format would reach for turn out not to be there.

Say that in the first three paragraphs, before any table.

## The sampling bias is understated and needs naming

The document says the sample is not random. It does not say how it is skewed, and the skew runs in the direction that matters.

Every query was a title search for a work named in advance: `alma.title="תלמוד בבלי"` and its like. That finds records catalogued under the title searched for, and systematically misses the records where the same work is expressed differently — a record whose 245 reads something else entirely and whose only statement of the work is a 130 uniform title is exactly the case the survey exists to find, and exactly the case a title search will not return.

So the corpus undercounts the variation it set out to measure, and the frequencies for the rarer treatments are lower bounds rather than estimates. That belongs beside the other cautions, stated plainly enough that nobody quotes a percentage as though it were a population figure.
close_reason: done

title: Compress HTTP responses
description:
`GZipMiddleware` is not in `MIDDLEWARE`, so no dynamic response is compressed. Whitenoise compresses static files only.

This matters more than it usually would because the heaviest pages are the ones a phone loads. The ingest workflow is explicitly phone-first — the phone is the camera, and the candidate list is reviewed on it — and cataloging happens at the shelves, where wifi is unreliable.

Concrete numbers, measured against a real 20-record NLI response while adding `source_marc` to candidates: the candidate results page is about 111 KB uncompressed and 15.3 KB gzipped. An ISBN lookup that hits NLI, LC and DNB at `max_records=20` could reach roughly 300 KB. Compression removes about 85% of that for one line of configuration.

## Shape

Add `django.middleware.gzip.GZipMiddleware` near the top of `MIDDLEWARE`, above the middleware whose output it should compress and in the position Django's documentation specifies.

Read the security note before doing it. Django's docs warn about the BREACH attack when compressing responses that contain both a CSRF token and attacker-controlled content. Django mitigates this by masking CSRF tokens per response, so the standard advice is that enabling it is safe, but the reasoning should be understood and stated rather than assumed. If it is not safe here, say why and close this rather than shipping it quietly.

Check whether anything downstream would double-compress once a real deployment exists (bd-n7a). A reverse proxy compressing an already-compressed response wastes work.
close_reason: Merged in PR #38

title: Attach the confirmed title-page image to the record and show it on the record page
description:
A title-page scan stores its photo on `ScanResult.image` under `media/staging/YYYY/MM/DD/`. Confirming the scan creates the Record through `_create_record_from_candidate` and leaves the image on the ScanResult; nothing moves it. `TitlePageImage` in `catalog/models.py` has a model with `upload_to="title-pages/%Y/%m/%d/"` and a `staged` flag, a migration and an admin inline, and no code creates one. So the photograph that identified the book stays a staging artifact instead of becoming part of the record. For a collection of old books, where the title page is the identity of the copy, that is the wrong outcome.

On confirm of an OCR scan, create a `TitlePageImage` for the new Record, move the file from staging to its permanent path through Django's storage API (so the code does not change if media moves to S3 under bd-n7a), set `staged=False`, and clear `ScanResult.image`. Show the image on the record page below the cover. The manual entry and edit form can gain an upload field for the same model afterwards; this ticket covers the scan path. E2e: confirm a title-page scan and see the image on the record page.
close_reason: done

title: Persist the title-statement fields when a candidate is confirmed
description:
The parser reads 245 `$n`, `$p` and `$c` and the `Record` model has `volume_part_number`, `volume_part_title` and `statement_of_responsibility`, but nothing writes them: `_create_record_from_candidate` was left untouched because another change owned `ingest/views.py` at the time. So the values show on candidate cards and are dropped the moment a record is created.

This is the remaining half of otzar-cex and the first half of otzar-55i.

## Shape

Three assignments on the `Record(...)` constructor in `_create_record_from_candidate`:

    volume_part_number=strip_marc_punctuation(candidate.get("volume_part_number")),
    volume_part_title=strip_marc_punctuation(candidate.get("volume_part_title")),
    statement_of_responsibility=strip_marc_punctuation(candidate.get("statement_of_responsibility")),

That one function serves both confirm entry points, `confirm_candidate` and `confirm_scan`, so there is nowhere else to change.

`strip_marc_punctuation` is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. The record page supplies its own ISBD colon between the part number and the part title, which assumes the stored values arrive without the cataloger's transcribed punctuation. Candidate dicts deliberately keep that punctuation; saved records deliberately do not.

## Testing

A unit test in `tests/test_ingest.py` asserting the three fields survive a confirm, and an e2e case that confirms a candidate and finds the values on the resulting record page.

## Not in scope

The role column on the record-author link populated from `700$e`/`$4` — the second half of otzar-55i, which needs its own relator-code mapping. And parsing roles out of `$c` prose, which otzar-55i rules out explicitly.
close_reason: done

title: The header overflows for a signed-in staff user on a narrow phone
description:
The header's utility row — theme toggle, GitHub link, Admin, username, Log out — extends past the viewport for a logged-in staff user at narrow widths. Measured at 320px: the row runs from x=139 to x=388 against a 320px viewport.

Its children measure 44 + 44 + 41 + 64 + 24 with four 8px gaps, so 249px of content in a row that starts 139px from the left. The outer bar itself fits — it measured 16..304 — so this is a child escaping its parent rather than the page being too wide.

That is the same failure as the search form on the home and search pages: a flex item defaults to `min-width: auto` and will not shrink below its content, so it overflows the container instead of compressing. The fix there was `min-w-0` on the element that should give way. Here nothing obviously should give way — every child is either an icon at its 44px touch target or a word.

## What was tried and did not work

Tightening the gap from `gap-4` to `gap-2` below the `sm` breakpoint. It applies — the computed `column-gap` is 8px — and the row still overflows, so the gaps were not what pushed it over.

The row cannot wrap instead: the bar is a fixed `h-16`, so a second line would overflow downward.

## Worth measuring before choosing a fix

Two probes of what should have been the same page disagreed about whether 375px overflows. That has to be resolved before trusting any fix, because it means one of the measurements was of something other than what it claimed. Fix the measurement first.

Candidates once it is understood: drop the username below `sm`, since a person knows who they are and it is the only child carrying no action; give the row `min-w-0` and let something truncate; or move the utility items into the same row as the search box, which already sits below the bar and has room.

## The regression test has a gap

`tests/e2e/test_site_chrome.py::TestNothingScrollsSideways` checks `/` and `/search/` at 320, 360, 375 and 414 and did not catch this, because it never logs in and the Admin link only renders for staff. Whatever fixes the layout should also make that test cover an authenticated staff user.

There is a second known gap in the same test. Scanning every element for one whose right edge escapes the viewport reports a false positive on the review queue, whose candidate table is deliberately wide inside an `overflow-x-auto` wrapper. An element inside a legitimately scrollable ancestor is not overflow, and the check should skip those rather than the queue being excluded from the test.
close_reason: done

title: Per-user activity view of records cataloged in a session
description:
A cataloger working through a shelf has no page that answers "what did I add today?" `Record.created_by` and `ScanResult.scanned_by` hold the data, `created_at` the times. A page under `/ingest/` listing the current user's records and scans grouped by day, newest first, with counts, gives a work session a visible result and a place to catch a mistaken confirm while it is fresh. Public browse pages stay as they are; this is a logged-in view.

Group by `timezone.localdate`, which follows `TIME_ZONE`; with UTC, evening work in the Americas lands on the next day's list.

title: Live phone-to-laptop barcode scanning flow
description:
When scanning barcodes on the phone via QR handoff, results should appear on the laptop in real-time instead of on the phone.

Current flow: phone scans barcode → results show on phone → confirm on phone.
Target flow: phone scans barcode → ScanResult created → laptop sees it immediately → confirm on laptop.

Implementation:

1. Phone scan page behavior change: after ISBN lookup returns candidates, create a ScanResult (scan_type='isbn') and show a simple 'Sent to review queue' confirmation instead of rendering candidates on the phone. Phone stays ready for the next scan.

2. Laptop scan page live updates: add an HTMX polling region (hx-trigger='every 3s') that checks for new pending ScanResults for the current user. When a new one arrives, render candidates inline on the scan page so the user can confirm/discard without navigating to the review queue.

4. After confirming a candidate on the laptop, the poll area resets to 'waiting for scans' and the phone can scan the next book.

5. Consider: should the phone auto-restart the camera after sending a scan? This would allow rapid scanning of multiple books.

Technical approach:
- New HTMX partial endpoint: GET /ingest/scan/poll/ returns pending ScanResults for current user as HTML fragment
- Laptop scan page includes a div with hx-get pointing to that endpoint, hx-trigger='every 3s'
- Phone scan page: detect if arrived via QR (e.g. session flag set by phone_scan_auth) and switch to 'scanner mode' — auto-submit to queue instead of rendering candidates

title: Offer existing author matches when confirming a scan
description:
`_create_record_from_candidate` in `ingest/views.py` creates authors with `Author.objects.get_or_create(name=author_name)`, and `_attach_from_candidate` does the same for additional authors. The same person arrives as `שניאור זלמן מלאדי` from NLI and `Shneur Zalman, of Lyady` from LC, so confirming two editions from two catalogs yields two Author rows, and the author browse page lists them apart. Every confirm through the ISBN path, the title-page path and the review queue takes this route, and nothing merges rows afterwards. This is the largest data-quality gap in the catalog and it compounds with every confirm.

`find_author_matches` in `ingest/authority.py` matches a name against existing authors by exact name, exact romanized name, or normalized variant-name form, and is called only from the `authority_check` endpoint the manual entry form uses. Call it in the confirm path with both the candidate's `author` and `author_alternate`; when it finds one strong match, attach that Author instead of creating one. When the match is ambiguous (several hits, or a hit by variant only) show a choice on the confirm page rather than picking silently; the queue's inline confirm can default to the strongest match and say which it chose.

When the candidate carries an alternate-script author form from an 880 field, store it on the Author row (`name_romanized` when the primary is Hebrew, `variant_names` otherwise) so later matches across scripts have something to hit. This is the local step; matching through VIAF identifiers is the parent ticket.

title: Call VIAF enrichment from the confirm path
description:
`enrich_author_from_viaf` and the `enrich_authors` management command landed, but nothing in the ingest flow calls them. An author created by confirming a scan gets no VIAF identifier and no variant forms until somebody runs the command by hand.

That matters because `otzar-1yn.1`'s local matcher reads `variant_names`: every enriched author makes the next confirm of that person match without asking. Enrichment left to a manual command is enrichment that mostly does not happen.

## The constraint the enrichment work recorded

A first VIAF lookup is one to four throttled requests, and only a repeat is served from the cache. Putting that in the confirm request would add seconds to the one interaction the workflow is built around. Django 6.1 ships `django.tasks` with only the immediate and dummy backends, so a "deferred" call would run inline anyway.

So this is blocked on a real background worker, or on accepting the latency, or on a third option nobody has costed yet. The hand-off point is recorded in the docstring of `enrich_author_from_viaf`: immediately after `resolve_candidate_author` creates a row.

## Also unwired

An `ambiguous` or `variant_only` outcome returns candidate matches that the confirm page does not offer. Those are exactly the cases a person should settle, and the local matcher already has a pattern for presenting that choice.

`docs/user-guide.md:210` tells users the app uses VIAF for variant spellings. That is true only after `enrich_authors` has been run, so either the wiring lands or the sentence needs qualifying.

## A host timer

The deployment offers the third option: a host timer, installed beside the snapshot timer, running `docker compose exec app python manage.py enrich_authors --limit N` nightly. The command already selects authors with no VIAF identifier, spaces requests by the configured delay and goes through the response cache. The confirm request stays fast and a newly created author is enriched within a day. It writes from a second process, which WAL mode and the 5 s busy timeout handle. It does not offer the ambiguous or variant-only outcomes to a person; that needs the confirm-path prompt or a review page for unresolved outcomes.

title: Auto-extract all MARC fields on record creation from catalog lookup
description:
When a record is created via ISBN lookup or OCR cascade (selecting a candidate), the full MARC record data should be extracted and saved to all related models — not just the few fields that go through the manual entry form.

Current problem: the ISBN lookup flow passes a handful of fields as GET params to the manual entry form. This loses: additional authors, subjects, series info, all external identifiers (LCCN, OCLC, etc.), the source MARC record itself, and the publication date from the 008 field.

Fix: when a candidate is selected (either from ISBN lookup _candidates.html or OCR results), the full parsed record data should be stored (e.g. in the session) and used to populate all related models on save. Specifically:

1. Store the full parsed record dict AND the raw marcjson in the session when a candidate is selected
2. On manual_entry form save, if session has candidate data:
   - Save source_marc (marcjson) and source_catalog on the Record
   - Extract and create ALL authors (not just the first) from MARC 100 and 700 fields
   - Extract and create subjects from MARC 650 fields
   - Extract publication date from MARC 008 or 260/264
   - Extract and save external identifiers (LCCN from 010, OCLC from 035, ISBN from 020)
   - Extract series info from 490/830
3. The manual entry form still allows the user to review and override, but defaults come from the MARC data

Files to modify:
- ingest/views.py (isbn_lookup_view, manual_entry)
- ingest/templates/ingest/_candidates.html (pass full parsed data, not just a few fields)
- sources/marc.py (may need to extract 700 additional authors, 010 LCCN, 035 OCLC)

title: Per-row HTMX lookup endpoint and live matrix updates
description:
Each row in the matrix view fires its own catalog lookup on load (browser-driven, one row at a time). Each completion swaps the row in place with its result.

## Endpoint

- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/lookup/`:
  - `@login_required`, ownership/staff check.
  - 409 if row.search_status not in `(pending, multiple)` (idempotent re-trigger only on pending/multiple).
  - Set `search_status=searching`, save.
  - Call `find_series_volume(series_title, author, row.volume_number)` (sibling bead bd-zx8).
  - Apply result:
    - 0 candidates → `search_status=no_match`.
    - 1 candidate → `search_status=found`, `candidate_records=[c]`, `selected_candidate_index=0`.
    - 2+ candidates → `search_status=multiple`, `candidate_records=cs`, `selected_candidate_index=0` (default to first; user can change).
  - Save and render the updated row partial.

## Matrix template

- `_series_claim_matrix.html` — wraps the table in a polling-friendly container.
- `_series_claim_row.html` — renders one row with status badge + candidate summary + per-row action buttons (skip / mark-held / pick-different placeholders rendered, behavior in next bead).

## Visual states per row

- `pending` — gray spinner, "queued"
- `searching` — blue spinner, "looking up..."
- `found` — green badge, candidate title + volume + source catalog
- `no_match` — yellow badge, "no match — saved as gap"
- `multiple` — yellow badge, candidate dropdown to pick

## Tests

- Unit: pending → searching → found transitions persist correctly.
- Unit: 409 on subsequent calls when not pending/multiple.
- Unit: cascade exception logs and leaves row in `searching` (or transitions to `no_match` — pick one in implementation; document choice).
- Auth: non-owner non-staff cannot trigger lookup.

## Dependencies

- bd-zx8 (per-volume lookup helper).
- bd-2t3 (model).
- bd-520 (form/create-claim endpoint, which renders the matrix).

Bead: bd-zwg (parent epic)

## One row at a time

Look up one row at a time. The deployment serves requests from eight threads (two gunicorn gthread workers of four), and each row lookup runs a catalog cascade inside its request: up to seven NLI steps plus the LC steps, each preceded by the `SRU_REQUEST_DELAY` sleep (3 s) and bounded by a 30 s timeout. A ten-volume claim with `hx-trigger="load"` on every row takes all eight threads for the length of its slowest cascades, and every other page waits behind it. The delay is a sleep inside each request, not a shared limiter, so parallel rows also send parallel queries to NLI and LC, the load the delay exists to prevent. Render the load trigger only on the first pending row, and have each row's response carry the trigger for the next pending row, so the matrix fills in order and holds one thread.

title: Consider gitignoring generated tailwind.css
description:
`static/css/tailwind.css` is a generated file committed to the repository. CI now exists, so the blocker this ticket was waiting on is gone.

This has already caused one user-visible bug. `ingest/templates/ingest/_notice.html` was added after the last stylesheet build, so `bg-amber-50` and `border-amber-300` were never compiled and the notice rendered with no background and no border. Nothing catches that: the template is valid, the tests pass, and the missing classes are invisible until someone looks at the page.

The failure mode is structural, not a one-off. A generated artifact under version control goes stale whenever a template adds a class and nobody rebuilds, and two branches that both rebuild produce a conflict in a file no one can meaningfully merge by hand.

## Shape

Gitignore the stylesheet and build it in CI and at deploy time. `just tailwind` already exists as the build step, and `catalog/templatetags/static_version.py` stamps the URL from the file's mtime, so a rebuilt file still busts caches.

Check what breaks first: the e2e suite renders real pages, so it needs the stylesheet present before Playwright runs, and the deploy path needs the same step.

## Second problem, same file

Tailwind is scanning `.beads/issues.jsonl`. `static/src/input.css` names four template directories with `@source`, but the scan still reaches the tracker export, so prose in bead descriptions leaks class candidates into the build. Constrain the sources so the stylesheet is derived from templates alone.
close_reason: Merged in PR #39

title: Data model: SeriesClaim and SeriesClaimRow with migration
description:
Introduce two new models tracking an in-progress series claim and its per-volume search rows. Keeping these separate from the persistent `Series` / `SeriesVolume` tables avoids polluting them with transient search/UI state.

## Models

```python
class SeriesClaim(models.Model):
    STATUS_CHOICES = [("pending", "Pending"), ("committed", "Committed"), ("cancelled", "Cancelled")]

    series = models.ForeignKey(Series, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True)
    created_by = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    resolved_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    volume_spec = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    originating_scan = models.ForeignKey("ingest.ScanResult", on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True)
    originating_volume_number = models.CharField(max_length=50, blank=True)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=STATUS_CHOICES, default="pending")


class SeriesClaimRow(models.Model):
    SEARCH_STATUS_CHOICES = [
        ("pending", "Pending"),
        ("searching", "Searching"),
        ("found", "Found"),
        ("no_match", "No match"),
        ("multiple", "Multiple matches"),
        ("manual_skip", "Skip"),
        ("manual_held", "Mark held"),
    ]

    claim = models.ForeignKey(SeriesClaim, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="rows")
    volume_number = models.CharField(max_length=50)
    search_status = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=SEARCH_STATUS_CHOICES, default="pending")
    candidate_records = models.JSONField(default=list, blank=True)
    selected_candidate_index = models.IntegerField(null=True, blank=True)
    created_record = models.ForeignKey("catalog.Record", on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["volume_number"]
        unique_together = [("claim", "volume_number")]
```

## Migration

- Auto-generate via `makemigrations`.
- No data migration; new tables only.

## Tests

- Unit: create a SeriesClaim with rows, verify cascade delete, unique constraint on (claim, volume_number).

## Dependencies

None blocking — can land in parallel with bd-cex / bd-j2k / bd-ra1.

Bead: bd-zwg (parent epic)

title: Capture volume evidence for multi-volume set records
description:
A photographed volume of a multi-volume set matches a catalog record for the whole set, and every trace of which volume it is gets dropped during parsing.

The Sapirstein Rashi record (LCCN 2001531851) identifies the volume in three fields, none of which the parser reads:

```
505 1  $a --   -- v. 3. Sefer Ṿa-yikṛa = Vayikra = Leviticus.
020    $a 9780899060286 $q (v. 3)
300    $a v. <3   > ; $c 26 cm.
440  4 $a The ArtScroll series
500    $a Sapirstein edition
```

`245` has no `$n` and no `$p` in this record, so reading the part subfields is not enough on its own: for an open-ended set held as one bibliographic record, the volume enumeration lives in the contents note, the ISBN qualifier, and the extent statement.

Capture the formatted contents note, the ISBN qualifier, and the extent statement, and show them on the record page. The volume identity is also known at ingest time — OCR read ויקרא off the title page — and is discarded at confirm, so the ingest side of this belongs with the series and volume work.

comments.author: dchud
comments.text: Reparented under bd-tz2s. The fields this ticket found — 440, 020 $q, 300 $a — are now in bd-tz2s.1's table, and the Sapirstein record is named there as a fixture. This ticket keeps the display half and the ingest-time loss of the volume identity that OCR already read.

title: Claim form on queue card and create-claim endpoint
description:
Add a "Claim series" affordance on each queue candidate that has series info; clicking opens a small form, parses the volume spec, persists the SeriesClaim and per-volume rows, and redirects to the matrix view.

## Changes

### Template
- `ingest/templates/ingest/_scan_poll.html` — for candidates with `series_title`, render an extra button alongside "Use this record": "Claim series of N volumes" or just "Claim as series" (label generic since N comes from the form).
- New partial `_claim_series_form.html` — a small inline form (HTMX-revealed below the candidate) with one text input ("Volumes you have"), a submit button, and a hint string explaining accepted syntax (`"1-5"`, `"all 5"`, `"1-2, 4-7, 10"`).

### Endpoint
- `POST /ingest/scan/<scan_id>/claim-series/`:
  - `@login_required`. The queue is no longer scoped per user, so there is no ownership check to make.
  - Read selected candidate index + volume spec.
  - Resolve the set the claim is about, and create a Record for the originating volume from the chosen candidate.
  - Parse the spec via existing `_parse_volume_spec` and record the volumes claimed but not yet held.
  - Create a `SeriesClaim` row with `originating_scan` set, and a `SeriesClaimRow` for each *non-originating* volume number with `search_status=pending`.
  - Redirect to `/ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/`.

**How the set is resolved and how a volume is recorded are deliberately not specified here.** This bead originally said to call `series_workflow.find_matching_series` and construct `SeriesVolume(series, record=None, volume_number=v, held=True)` directly. Both are being replaced: `bd-tz2s.3` gives a set an identity established from accumulated evidence rather than from one record's title, makes the volume designation nullable, and replaces `unique_together` with a constraint conditioned on a designation existing. Writing this against the old shape means writing it twice, which is why this bead now blocks on that one.

Use whatever the identity work settles on. If that work has not settled a question this needs answered, that is a finding worth reporting rather than routing around.

### The claim must not be offered for a publisher's imprint

`490` and `830` carry two different kinds of thing. `Talmud Bavli` is a work whose volumes somebody sets out to complete; `ArtScroll series` is a publisher's label attached to unrelated books. "Claim series of N volumes" is a sensible offer for the first and nonsense for the second — nobody holds volume 3 of ArtScroll, and claiming five of them would manufacture exactly the meaningless gap placeholders `bd-vh3n` exists to prevent.

The affordance appears only where the candidate's series is a work. That is why this bead blocks on `bd-vh3n` as well.

### Matrix render (initial)
- `GET /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/` — render a table with one row per `SeriesClaimRow`, each row in the "pending" state with an HTMX `hx-trigger="load"` on `/ingest/series-claim/.../row/<row_id>/lookup/` (implemented in the next bead).

## Tests

- Unit: POST with a valid spec creates Series + SeriesVolumes + SeriesClaim + SeriesClaimRow per expected volume.
- Unit: spec parsing rejects malformed input (returns to form with error).
- Unit: existing Series is reused (no duplicate Series for the same title).
- Unit: matrix view requires login + ownership.

## Dependencies

- bd-j2k (Series persistence on confirm — same Series-creation helper).
- bd-pb6 (data model — SeriesClaim and SeriesClaimRow tables).

title: Record author roles and the statement of responsibility
description:
Author roles are not recorded anywhere. The record-to-author link (`Record.authors` through table) holds only the record and author ids, and `parse_record` reads `245` subfields `$a` and `$b` only, so the statement of responsibility in `$c` is discarded.

For the Sapirstein Rashi volume (LCCN 2001531851), the roles exist in exactly one place in the LC record:

```
245 10 $a [Perush Rashi ʻal ha-Torah] = $b Rashi : the Torah : with Rashi's commentary / $c translated, annotated, and elucidated by Yisrael Isser Zvi Herczeg ; in collaboration with Yaakov Petroff and Yoseph Kamenetsky ; contributing editor, Avie Gold.
700 1  $a Herczeg, Yisrael Isser Zvi.
700 1  $a Petroff, Yaakov.
700 1  $a Kamenetzky, Yosef.
700 1  $a Gold, Avie.
```

The `700` fields carry no `$e` relator term and no `$4` relator code, so no parser can derive the roles from them — the four contributors arrive flat and indistinguishable, and the catalog page lists them alongside Rashi as if all five stood in the same relation to the book.

Two pieces of work, either useful alone:

Transcribe `245$c` into a statement-of-responsibility field on `Record` and show it under the title. This is what the field is for, it needs no interpretation, and it answers "who did what" for a reader.

## The staging sweep

`cleanup_staging` treats every file under `staging/` that no `ScanResult.image` references as an orphan and deletes it after the retention period (`referenced_image_names`), and bd-dovi runs it with `--apply` on a schedule. title: Add GitHub link and build state indicator to site chrome
description:
Surface a link to the otzar GitHub repo (https://github.com/dchud/otzar) and a small build/state indicator in the site chrome.

## Scope

1. **GitHub link** — add to the header nav (top-right area in templates/base.html, near the dark-mode toggle and auth controls) and/or the footer. Header placement is preferred for visibility; footer is a fine fallback if the header gets crowded.

2. **Build/state indicator in the footer** (templates/base.html) — show:
   - Short commit SHA (first 7 chars) of `HEAD` at deploy/build time.
   - Branch name if not `main`.
   - A version/tag if one is present (`git describe --tags --always`).
   - Link the SHA to the corresponding commit on GitHub (e.g. `https://github.com/dchud/otzar/commit/<sha>`).

## Implementation notes

- Resolve git info at startup, not per request. Options:
  - A management command or build step writes `otzar/_build_info.py` (or similar) with constants the template can read via a context processor.

- Local dev should still work when git info is unavailable — fall back to showing nothing or just "dev".
- For Fly.io / Docker deploys, the Dockerfile/entrypoint can capture git metadata into env vars or a generated file at build time. See `Dockerfile` and `entrypoint.sh` for the right hook point.

## Acceptance

- Header (or footer) shows a GitHub link that opens the repo in a new tab.
- Footer shows commit SHA (linked to GitHub), branch (if non-main), and tag (if present).
- Works in local dev (gracefully degrades when git metadata is missing).
- Works in deployed environment (commit SHA reflects the actually-deployed commit).

title: Defer OCR in title_page_upload and add run_ocr endpoint
description:
Decouple title-page image upload from OCR execution. The upload step saves the image and creates a `ScanResult` in `awaiting_ocr`; a new `run_ocr` endpoint runs Claude Vision on demand and returns the existing edit-metadata partial.

## Changes

- `ingest/views.py::title_page_upload` (modify):
  - Save uploaded image bytes to `ScanResult.image` (Django ImageField; existing `staging/%Y/%m/%d/` upload_to).
  - Status `awaiting_ocr`, `ocr_output=None`, `candidate_records=[]`.
  - Do NOT call `extract_metadata_from_image`.
  - Stop writing to `tmp/title_pages/<uuid>.jpg` (redundant once `ScanResult.image` is the source of truth).
  - Phone-mode response (`request.session.get("phone_scan_target") == "title"`): render a small "sent" partial that shows the uploaded image plus Run OCR / Retake controls.
  - Desktop-mode response: render the new `_title_page_poll.html` card partial (the desktop pane will swap it in).
- `ingest/urls.py` — add `path("scan-title/<int:scan_id>/ocr/", views.run_ocr, name="run_ocr")`.
- `ingest/views.py::run_ocr` (NEW):
  - `@login_required`, `@require_POST`, ownership/staff check.
  - 409 if `scan.status != "awaiting_ocr"`.
  - Read image bytes via `scan.image.read()`; call `extract_metadata_from_image`.
  - On success: set `scan.status = "pending"`, `scan.ocr_output = metadata`, save. Render existing `_ocr_results.html` (which already supports the metadata edit + cascade-search step).
  - On `extract_metadata_from_image` returning None: leave `awaiting_ocr`; return error partial inline (with retry-and-discard affordances).

## Tests

- Upload phase: creates `ScanResult` with image saved, status `awaiting_ocr`, no OCR called (mock at the import boundary, since `pytest-socket` blocks live HTTP).
- `run_ocr` happy path: state transitions correctly, ocr_output populated, partial rendered.
- `run_ocr` 409 on already-processed.
- `run_ocr` OCR-None: state unchanged, error partial rendered.
- Auth check on both endpoints.

## Dependencies

Depends on the `awaiting_ocr` status bead (so the status value exists).

Bead: bd-xh6 (parent epic)

title: JavaScript barcode scanning from camera
description:
Add real-time barcode scanning via the phone/laptop camera to the ISBN scan page (ingest/templates/ingest/isbn_scan.html).

Current state: The page has a manual ISBN text input that POSTs to the isbn_lookup HTMX endpoint. The camera viewfinder area shows a placeholder message.

Implementation:

1. Add a JavaScript barcode library. Two options:
   - Barcode Detection API (navigator.ml.barcodeDetector): native in Chrome and Safari on mobile, zero dependencies, but not available in Firefox. Check for support and fall back gracefully.
   - QuaggaJS (or its maintained fork @nicolo-ribaudo/quagga2): works everywhere, heavier (~100KB). Use as fallback when Barcode Detection API is unavailable.

   Recommendation: try Barcode Detection API first, fall back to QuaggaJS.

2. Camera access: use navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ video: { facingMode: 'environment' } }) to get the rear camera on phones. Display the live feed in a <video> element in the viewfinder area.

5. Permissions UX: if camera permission is denied, show a clear message and keep the manual input available as fallback. The manual ISBN input should always remain visible below the camera viewfinder.

6. Mobile considerations: the camera viewfinder should be large enough to frame a barcode easily (~300x200px minimum). Add a torch/flashlight toggle button if the browser supports it (via MediaStreamTrack.applyConstraints with torch: true).

7. The JS can be inline in the template or in a separate static file (static/js/barcode-scan.js). Keep it simple — no build step.

title: Capture bookplate, stamp and dedication images
description:
The three ownership-mark tickets under this epic landed the text half: `provenance`, `bookplate_text`, `dedication_text` and `stamp_text` are on `Record`, in the confirm and edit forms, in `FTS_TEXT_COLUMNS`, and rendered on the record page.

The image half is not built and is not tracked anywhere. `Record` has no image field for any of these marks; the only `ImageField` in `catalog/models.py` is the title page, and the only other is the staged scan in `ingest/models.py`. Two of the epic's stated goals depend on it: a consistent model for optional text **and image** metadata, and phone camera capture across every image-capable element.

## What it needs

A single shape covering all three marks rather than three near-identical fields — a bookplate, a stamp and a dedication are the same thing to the data model, and a copy can carry several of each. That argues for a related model with a mark type, an image, and the transcribed text, rather than more columns on `Record`. Consider whether the existing `_text` columns fold into it or stay put; folding them means a data migration and re-deriving the FTS rows, so it needs deciding rather than assuming.

Capture reuses the title-page path. Photographing a bookplate on a phone is the same act as photographing a title page, and the staged-image and handoff machinery already exists; a second, parallel upload path would be the wrong answer.

Rendering follows the epic's rule: images below the cover, text below the primary metadata, the whole block absent when there is nothing to show.

## Why it is separate from the three closed tickets

Those delivered what a cataloger can type. This is what they can photograph, and it is the part that makes a mark verifiable by someone who was not holding the book.

## The staging sweep

A mark photograph staged under `staging/` by anything other than `ScanResult.image` is deleted by the scheduled sweep as an orphan (`referenced_image_names` in `cleanup_staging.py`). Either stage it as a `ScanResult`, which is the reuse this ticket asks for, or extend that reference set. The permanent image goes through the storage API under its own prefix, like `title-pages/` and `covers/`, which puts it in the versioned media bucket with no provisioning change.

title: Normalize publisher strings before catalog search queries
description:
The publisher string extracted by OCR goes into the CQL query verbatim, and exact-phrase matching against the catalog's publisher index is sensitive to corporate suffixes and punctuation. A title page reading "Mesorah Publications, Ltd." produces a query that matches nothing, so the `title+publisher` step returns empty and `run_cascade` falls through to the broad title-only step. The publisher is effectively ignored and the candidate list is dominated by unrelated editions.

Measured against NLI SRU with the same title:

```
alma.title="ויקרא" AND alma.publisher="Mesorah Publications, Ltd."   0 hits
alma.title="ויקרא" AND alma.publisher="Mesorah Publications"         2 hits
alma.title="ויקרא" AND alma.publisher="Mesorah"                      2 hits
alma.title="ויקרא" AND alma.publisher="ArtScroll"                    1 hit
```

Add a normalization helper in `sources/cascade.py` that strips trailing corporate suffixes (Ltd, Ltd., Inc., LLC, GmbH) and trailing punctuation before a publisher value is formatted into a CQL template, and apply it in the cascade steps that use `{publisher}`. Unit tests should cover the suffix forms, a publisher that needs no change, and confirmation that an empty result after normalization still falls through rather than erroring.

Consider whether a `publisher+keywords` step belongs in the cascade for multi-volume works, where the volume title on the title page is not the catalog title: the Sapirstein edition volume photographed as ויקרא is cataloged as "Rashi : the Torah : with Rashi's commentary", so no title-constrained query can reach it, while `alma.publisher="Mesorah Publications" AND alma.all_for_ui="Rashi"` returns it.
close_reason: Merged in PR #14

title: Volume number normalization helper for series matching
description:
Provide a helper that maps a volume designation (as it appears in MARC 490\$v / 830\$v / 245\$n) to a canonical form for cross-record comparison. Needed so the per-volume catalog lookup can match results back to user-specified volume numbers.

## Surface forms to handle

- Arabic digits: "3", "v. 3", "vol. 3", "volume 3", "pt. 3", "no. 3"
- Roman numerals: "iii", "III", "vol. III"
- Hebrew letters / gematria: "ג", "חלק ג", "ספר ג", "כרך ג", "ה" → 5
- Whole-text mixed: "ספר ג: משפטים" (volume + part title; we only want the number)

## API

```python
def normalize_volume_number(raw: str) -> str:
    """Return a canonical Arabic-digit string for the volume number, or "" if unparseable."""
```

Examples:
- `"v. 3"` → `"3"`
- `"III"` → `"3"`
- `"חלק ג"` → `"3"`
- `"כרך ה: ספר אהבה"` → `"5"`
- `""` or unparseable → `""`

## Implementation notes

- Strip common prefixes ("vol.", "v.", "pt.", "no.", "חלק", "ספר", "כרך", "כתב", "מהדורה") before parsing.
- Try Arabic-digit regex first, then Roman numerals, then gematria.
- Gematria limited to volumes 1..200 is fine (real series dont go higher); table-based mapping rather than full gematria solver.

## Tests

- Pure unit tests in `tests/test_marc_cleanup.py` or a new `tests/test_volume_numbers.py`.
- Cover all four surface forms above, plus edge cases (empty, all-text, leading/trailing whitespace).

title: Per-row override actions and final commit endpoint
description:
Once the matrix has run all its lookups, the user reviews each row, makes overrides, and clicks Commit to finalize. This bead adds the per-row controls and the commit endpoint.

## Per-row endpoints

- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/select/?index=N` — change the chosen candidate (when search_status=multiple). Updates `selected_candidate_index`. Returns the row partial.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/skip/` — set `search_status=manual_skip`. Returns the row partial.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/mark-held/` — set `search_status=manual_held` (i.e. user has the volume but no record can be found; will land as a gap-with-`held=True` placeholder).
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/retry/` — reset to `pending`; trigger a fresh lookup (frontend fires the lookup endpoint after re-render).

## Commit endpoint

- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/commit/`:
  - `@login_required`, ownership/staff check.
  - Refuse if any row is still `pending` or `searching`.
  - For each row:
    - `found` (or `multiple` with a `selected_candidate_index`): create a Record from the chosen candidate using `_attach_from_candidate`. Update the matching `SeriesVolume(series, volume_number=row.volume_number)` to point at the new Record. Set `row.created_record`.
    - `no_match` or `manual_held`: leave the SeriesVolume placeholder as-is (`record=None, held=True`).
    - `manual_skip`: delete the SeriesVolume for that volume_number (user retracted the claim for this one).
  - Set `claim.status=committed`, `claim.resolved_at=now`.
  - Redirect to the originating Series detail page (or the series_manage view).

## UI

- Each row shows action buttons appropriate to its state (Pick alternate / Skip / Mark held / Retry).
- A single "Commit claim" button at the bottom is disabled while any row is pending or searching.

## Tests

- Unit: each per-row action transitions state correctly and is idempotent.
- Unit: commit creates Records, links SeriesVolumes, sets claim status; refuses while anything pending.
- Unit: skip retracts the SeriesVolume for that number.

- Token with `title` target → redirects to title_page_scan, sets session flag.
