title: Phone-to-desktop handoff for title page scanning
description:
Add a QR-driven phone-to-desktop handoff for the title-page scan ingest path, mirroring the existing barcode/ISBN scan flow. The user opens /ingest/scan-title/ on their laptop, scans a QR code with their phone to authenticate and land on a streamlined capture UI, takes a title-page photo, and reviews the image — from either device — before OCR runs. Confirmation kicks off OCR and proceeds into the existing edit-metadata + cascade-search workflow.

## Goals

- Smooth desktop → phone → camera → desktop loop with one tap each side.
- Image is reviewed (and can be discarded/retaken) before OCR tokens are spent.
- Either device can confirm or discard; the other catches up via polling.
- The existing direct-upload path on desktop stays as an alternative.

## High-level flow

```
Desktop /ingest/scan-title/  ──QR──►  Phone /phone-auth/<token>/
                                           │ sets phone_scan_target=title
                                           ▼
                                      Phone scan-title (streamlined)
                                           │ take photo, upload
                                           ▼
                                  ScanResult.image saved, status=awaiting_ocr
                                           │
                  ┌────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┐
                  ▼                                                 ▼
         Desktop poll: image card                       Phone shows image card
         [Run OCR] [Discard]                            [Run OCR] [Retake]
                  │
                  ▼
        Either side: Run OCR ──► OCR runs, status=pending,
                                 ocr_output set, edit-metadata UI shown
                                 (existing cascade search continues)

        Either side: Discard ──► image file deleted, status=discarded
                                 (confirmation prompt before delete)
```

## Data model

Extend `ScanResult.STATUS_CHOICES` with a new value `awaiting_ocr` (OCR-only):

| Status         | image | ocr_output | candidate_records | Meaning                                     |
|----------------|-------|------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| awaiting_ocr   | set   | NULL       | []                | (NEW) Image uploaded, OCR not yet run       |
| pending        | set   | set        | populated         | OCR done, awaiting record selection         |
| confirmed      | —     | —          | —                 | Record created                              |
| discarded      | NULL  | —          | —                 | Rejected; image file deleted, row kept      |

Image storage moves from `tmp/title_pages/<uuid>.jpg` to `ScanResult.image` via the existing `ImageField` (already configured for `staging/%Y/%m/%d/`). DB migration required.

## URLs / views

| URL                                      | View                       | Notes |
|------------------------------------------|----------------------------|-------|
| `GET /ingest/qr/?target=title`           | `qr_code_view` (extended)  | Token signs `<user_pk>:<target>`; target ∈ {isbn, title}. |
| `GET /ingest/phone-auth/<token>/`        | `phone_scan_auth` (ext.)   | Sets `phone_scan_target` session key; redirects accordingly. |
| `GET /ingest/scan-title/`                | `title_page_scan` (ext.)   | Renders desktop (QR sidebar + poll pane) or phone (streamlined) variant. |
| `POST /ingest/upload-title/`             | `title_page_upload` (chg.) | Defers OCR. Saves image to `ScanResult.image`, status=awaiting_ocr. Returns phone confirmation in phone mode, image-card partial otherwise. |
| `GET /ingest/scan-title/poll/`           | `title_page_poll` (NEW)    | Returns image cards for the current users awaiting_ocr scans. Polled by desktop and phone. |
| `POST /ingest/scan-title/<id>/ocr/`      | `run_ocr` (NEW)            | Runs OCR on saved image, transitions to pending, returns existing `_ocr_results.html` partial. 409 if already processed. |
| `POST /ingest/scan-title/<id>/discard/`  | `discard_title_scan` (NEW) | Deletes image file (`scan.image.delete(save=False)`), status=discarded. Idempotent. `hx-confirm` on the trigger. |

All write endpoints use `@login_required` and check `scan.scanned_by == request.user or request.user.is_staff`.

## QR token format

Currently signs `str(user_pk)`. Extend to `f"{user_pk}:{target}"`. Backwards compatible: tokens missing the target default to `isbn` so any in-flight QR keeps working.

## UI

**Desktop `/ingest/scan-title/`** (when not phone_scanner):
- Existing direct upload form retained.
- New right sidebar with QR code (mirrors barcode page; `target=title`).
- New "Incoming photos" pane polling `title_page_poll` every 3s.
- Each pending scan: thumbnail + Run OCR / Discard buttons. Discard uses `hx-confirm="Discard this photo?"`.
- Run OCR swaps the card with the existing edit-metadata partial; the cascade-search flow takes over from there unchanged.

**Phone `/ingest/scan-title/`** (when `phone_scan_target=title`):
- Streamlined capture using the existing `<input capture="environment">` UI.
- After upload, replaces form with image card + Run OCR / Retake. Retake calls discard then re-renders capture.
- Lightweight poll on the same endpoint to detect desktop action and avoid stale UI.

## Reuse vs new

- `_scan_poll.html` polling pattern is reused with a new template `_title_page_poll.html` for image cards.
- `_ocr_results.html` partial unchanged — `run_ocr` returns it directly so the cascade-search step is identical to today.
- New `discard_title_scan` rather than overloading existing `discard_scan` (which has ISBN-flow-coupled redirects).

## Error handling & edge cases

- **Upload failure**: phone shows inline error, capture stays available, no partial `ScanResult` created.
- **OCR failure** (`extract_metadata_from_image` returns None): scan stays in `awaiting_ocr`; card shows error with Retry / Discard.
- **Race (both devices act)**: last write wins. `run_ocr` returns 409 if no longer in `awaiting_ocr`. `discard` is idempotent. Both polls reconcile.
- **Token expiry / wrong target**: `TimestampSigner` already validates max_age=3600. Missing target → isbn (back-compat). Unknown target → 400.
- **Image cleanup**: `scan.image.delete(save=False)` on disk; `image=None`, `status=discarded` in DB; row kept for audit.
- **Stale awaiting_ocr rows**: out of scope for v1; consider a janitor command later.
- **Phone session conflict**: `phone_scan_target` overwritten on each `phone-auth` hit.

## Testing

Per CLAUDE.md, user-visible workflow changes require Playwright e2e coverage.

**Unit tests** (`ingest/tests.py`):
- QR token round-trip (valid, expired, malformed, missing target → isbn default).
- Deferred-upload: status=awaiting_ocr, image saved, OCR not invoked.
- `run_ocr`: happy path, 409 on already-processed, OCR-None error, auth check.
- `discard_title_scan`: file deleted, status set, idempotent, auth check.
- `title_page_poll`: returns only requesting users awaiting_ocr scans.

**E2e tests** (`tests/e2e/`):
- Two browser contexts (desktop + phone); phone navigates a generated `phone-auth` URL.
- Phone uploads fixture title-page image → desktop poll → desktop Run OCR (Claude Vision patched at boundary, since `pytest-socket` blocks live HTTP) → metadata edit → cascade search (also patched) → record created.
- Phone uploads → desktop discards (with confirm) → image gone, status=discarded, phone poll reverts to capture.

Fixture: small JPG under `tests/fixtures/title_pages/`, no real bibliographic content.

## Out of scope (potential follow-ups)

- Multi-page (title + verso) capture and merged OCR.
- Janitor command to prune stale awaiting_ocr rows.
- In-browser rotation / cropping before OCR.
- Phone landing screen offering both barcode and title-page capture from one QR.

## Child beads

This epic is implemented through these child beads (created with this epic):
1. Extend QR/auth flow to support per-target scan landing.
2. Add awaiting_ocr status + use ScanResult.image for title-page uploads.
3. Defer OCR in title_page_upload; add run_ocr endpoint.
4. Add title_page_poll view and image-card partial.
5. Update scan-title template: desktop QR sidebar + poll pane; phone streamlined view.
6. Add discard_title_scan endpoint with image cleanup + confirmation.
7. E2e Playwright test for full handoff flow.

title: Series-aware ingest with auto-fetch and matrix review
description:
When a scanned volume is part of a multi-volume series, let the user claim the whole set (or any subset) in one action. The system auto-fetches sibling volumes from the source catalogs, presents a live-updating matrix the user can review and override row-by-row, then commits the accepted records and links them to a single Series with appropriate SeriesVolume entries.

Builds on existing infrastructure: `Series`, `SeriesVolume(record nullable, held bool)`, `series_workflow.create_series_volumes` (already parses "1-5" / "all 5" / "1-2, 4-7, 10").

Originally raised in feedback from @shalomhav on issue #4 (https://github.com/dchud/otzar/issues/4) and refined in conversation about volume-3-of-5 cases where one record carries the volume designation but the total is only known to the user.

## User flow

1. User scans an ISBN; queue surfaces candidates from NLI/LC/etc as today.
2. A candidate with series info shows a new "Claim series" affordance alongside "Use this record".
3. Click opens a small form: "Volumes you have" (text input parsed as range/list/all-N).
4. Submit:
   - Match or create the `Series` (by title + author normalization).
   - Create a `Record` for the originally-scanned volume from the chosen candidate.
   - Create `SeriesVolume` placeholders (`held=True, record=None`) for all other volume numbers in the spec.
   - Persist a `SeriesClaim` row tracking which volumes are still being searched.
5. Redirect to the matrix view. Each row triggers its own HTMX-driven catalog search on load (browser-driven, one row at a time; see otzar-2ao).
6. Each row updates live: pending → searching → "found candidate(s)" / "no match" / "multiple — pick one".
7. User reviews and edits per-row (skip, choose alternate candidate, mark as gap-only).
8. Single "Commit" button creates Records for accepted candidates, links them to their SeriesVolumes, and resolves the claim.

## Honest caveats baked into the UX

- Each auto-fetch is best-effort and the matrix shows the candidate so the user can veto.

- **Searching by series title and filtering on `490$v`/`830$v` is weaker than this bead originally assumed.** A survey of 1,027 records, written up in `docs/marc-in-practice.md`, found `490` and `830` on 3% of records published before 1970 against 24% and 17% after 1990. The uniform title runs the other way: most common on the oldest records, and for something like the 1895 Vilna Talmud it is the only field on the record that names the work at all. A sibling search that keys on the series statement finds nothing for exactly the material this collection is heaviest in. `otzar-zx8` is written against the stronger signals and is the bead that settles this; this one should not contradict it.

- **A pre-1970 volume has no ISBN.** Not rarely — never, in 279 surveyed records, because ISO 2108 postdates the printing. Any sibling search that starts from an identifier is unavailable for the older half of a collection, and title-and-author matching is all there is.

- Volume numbers come in Arabic digits, Hebrew letters and gematria, and Roman numerals — but more often than any of those, in this material, the designation is a *name*: Pesahim, Rosh ha-shanah, פרה. `130 $p`, `240 $p` and `730 $p` together appear on more records than every numeric designation in the corpus combined. A matrix keyed on parsed integers cannot represent most of what it will meet.
- Some volumes wont be in any catalog. Those stay as `held=True, record=None` placeholders.
- Each row lookup holds one of the application's eight request threads for the length of its cascade, so rows are looked up one at a time.

## Data model additions

- New `SeriesClaim` model — transient (or kept-for-audit) tracking of an in-progress claim:
  - `series` (FK, nullable until matched)
  - `created_by`, `created_at`, `resolved_at`
  - `volume_spec` (raw user input string)
  - `originating_scan` (FK to ScanResult)
  - `originating_volume_number` (string)
  - `status` (pending / committed / cancelled)
- New `SeriesClaimRow` (one per volume in the spec):
  - `claim` (FK)
  - `volume_number` (string)
  - `search_status` (pending / searching / found / no_match / multiple / manual_skip / manual_held)
  - `candidate_records` (JSONField — same shape as `ScanResult.candidate_records`)
  - `selected_candidate_index` (nullable int)
  - `created_record` (nullable FK)

This keeps the persistent `Series`/`SeriesVolume` model clean: claims and their per-volume search state live separately and can be discarded after commit.

## Architecture / endpoints (sketch — child beads refine)

- `POST /ingest/scan/<scan_id>/claim-series/` — create the SeriesClaim and SeriesVolume placeholders; redirect to matrix.
- `GET /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/` — render the matrix.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/lookup/` — run the catalog search for one row; HTMX fires this on row load. Returns the updated row partial.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/row/<row_id>/select/` — user picks an alternate candidate or marks skip/held.
- `POST /ingest/series-claim/<claim_id>/commit/` — finalize.

## Volume number matching

Need a `normalize_volume_number(s) -> str` helper that maps Hebrew letters and gematria, Roman numerals, and Arabic digits to a canonical form for comparison. (See bd children for details.)

## Out of scope (potential follow-ups)

- @shalomhavs "keep scanning more volumes from the same series" UX — auto-detect on subsequent ISBN scans that we already have a Series for this title, offer to attach. Distinct ergonomics from the claim-the-set workflow; lower priority once auto-fetch ships.
- Rate-limit-aware sequential search (current model is browser-driven fan-out, parallel).
- Series authority enrichment. Note that `800`, `810` and `811` appear **zero** times in the 1,027-record survey, across three catalogs and three eras, so disambiguating through them would be building against a treatment these endpoints do not send for this material.

## Child beads

1. Surface volume part metadata (245$n / 245$p) in MARC parser, candidates, queue.
2. Persist Series + SeriesVolume on single-scan confirm.
3. Volume number normalization helper (Hebrew / gematria / Roman / Arabic).
4. Per-volume catalog lookup helper.
5. Data model: SeriesClaim + SeriesClaimRow + migration.
6. Claim form on queue card + create-claim endpoint + initial matrix render.
7. Per-row HTMX lookup endpoint + live matrix updates.
8. Per-row override actions + final commit endpoint.
9. E2e Playwright test for the full claim flow with patched cascades.

title: Per-volume catalog lookup helper
description:
A helper that, given a set and a target volume, queries the source-catalog cascade and returns ranked candidates for that volume. The value is filling gaps: a collection holds volumes 1, 2 and 5 of a set and wants 3 and 4 found without retyping the search each time.

## Why this needs specifying against varied practice

The obvious implementation searches by series title and filters candidates on `normalize_volume_number` of their `490 $v` or `830 $v`, discarding anything without one. That fails on most of the variation this catalog will meet: a multipart monograph carries its designation in `245 $n`, an analytic in `773 $g`, a set catalogued without numbering carries none at all, and a tractate is often identified by name rather than by number in the first place.

Filtering on one field means the volumes hardest to find are the ones the helper refuses to return.

## Shape

Query by the strongest set identifier available rather than by title alone — uniform title where the set has one, authorized series title otherwise, transcribed title as a fallback. Scope to a catalog's series or uniform-title index where the SRU target supports one, and fall back to a general title search where it does not.

Match a candidate's volume against the target using every designation the record carries, not one field: `490 $v`, `830 $v`, `245 $n`, `773 $g`, and the part title in `245 $p` where the "number" is a name — Berakhot rather than 1.

Rank rather than filter. A candidate whose set matches and whose designation cannot be read is worth showing below the confident matches, because the person looking at it can tell in a second what the parser cannot. Returning nothing is the worse failure: the user cannot tell a genuine absence from a parser that did not understand the record.

## Tests

Mocked cascade returning candidates that express the same volume four different ways; all four match. A candidate from a different set with the same volume number does not. A candidate with no readable designation is ranked low rather than dropped. Cascade exceptions are logged and yield an empty list rather than raising.
